what: The thirty rooms the suite is merging down to, and what each one absorbs. Hand-authored, not generated. test/run.js checks it against shared/registry.js on every run, so the map cannot quietly drift from the app.

howToRead.survivors: One entry per surviving room. 'id' is its registry id and stays its id; 'title' is what it is called after the merge (the registry may still carry the old title until that merge ships).
howToRead.absorbs: Registry ids that become a view, a toggle, a block type or a card inside the survivor. Every one of them ends as a redirect file, never a deleted file: the links are out in the world.
howToRead.done: The subset of 'absorbs' that has already been retired. A room in 'done' must be a redirect and must be gone from the registry; a room in 'absorbs' but not 'done' must still be a live registry room. That pair is the drift alarm.
howToRead.held: Absorbed rooms that are deliberately NOT being retired yet, each with the reason. A held room stays live until the reason is cleared.
howToRead.order: The six sessions the plan sequenced, not the whole job: they are the merges whose ORDER matters. Every other absorption in this file is independent of them and can be taken in any session, one at a time. Reading 'four of six shipped' as 'two sessions left' is the misreading this line exists to stop.

rules: Same fields, different framing is one room with a toggle, not two rooms.
Before and after of one decision is one room with a time axis.
A lens is a toggle, not a room.
A single fact is a card inside the room where that fact changes a decision.
ANTI-RULE, and it outranks the five: a room with a different emotional register does not merge, even when the math is identical.

rooms.title: The Number

rooms.title: The Cushion
rooms.note: Four readings of one number: how long can you not earn. The toggle is the insight; four rooms hid it.

rooms.title: What The Next Dollar Does
rooms.note: One question at three amounts. The FOO step number stays visible everywhere.

rooms.title: The Decision Room

held.wedding: The shell is built and Reversibility is a field on every block (D-253). The wedding is the next block TYPE, and it is more than a goal template: the per-guest slider that prices one more table in days of FI is the thing people actually use it for, and it needs a block type that carries a per-unit figure. That is a session, not a paragraph.
held.what-if-life: A deep module, in STATUS.md's own sequencing: one event in three versions (dream, default, disaster) is three blocks that have to be read together, which the shell cannot yet do.
held.worth: Different register, and the anti-rule applies: every other block is a decision ahead of you, and Worth It is a judgement about one behind you. It is about regret, not choice. It wants its own look before it is folded in.
held.hassle: A chore that pays per hour is a block whose cost is negative and whose unit is your time, not money. The shell prices what things COST; this one needs the shell to price what a thing PAYS before it can move.
held.adventure: A deep module: every way through five years on a card each, with a crash or a lost job thrown at it. That is a scenario walker over blocks, and the shell has to be able to hold a block before it can walk a set of them.
held.timeline: A period of future income is not a decision you are weighing; it is a fact about a calendar. It may belong with Income or The Month rather than here, and that is the owner's call.

rooms.note: One shell, many block types; five outputs on every block. Reversibility becomes a field on every block, not a room.

rooms.title: Housing
rooms.note: The house hack (D-225) already ships inside this room; it never became a room of its own. The Deal (D-227) arrived on main after this map was written and is named here by rule 1: it and Housing sit on the same engines/ownership.js arithmetic and differ in framing — whether a building pays, against whether to buy where you live. Naming it is not a verdict on shipping it; it is what the map is for.

rooms.title: Wheels
rooms.note: Same car, same 20/3/8 test, same table, asked at two depths. The check is the default because someone who wants a yes or no should not have to read a depreciation curve to find one.

rooms.title: Work

held.rollover: Every other room on this page carries appliesWhen "situation != retired"; The Account You Left Behind never did, because it sits in Your Numbers rather than in Work. Folding it in would take it from the people most likely to have left a plan behind. It wants a different home — The Statement's where-it-lands reading is the candidate, per D-228 — or a per-reading situation rule, and that is the owner's call rather than a session's.

rooms.note: Seven old rooms, every one about a job. Nothing here is about building something that pays you; that gap is now more visible, not less.

rooms.title: When It Won't All Get Paid
